title: A Special Episode for Kids: The Fear Facer

sentences.en: Well, what's that?
That?
My dream catcher?
Oh, it's called a dream catcher, so I guess it, like, catches bad dreams, but it hasn't been working so good.
sentences.zh: 哦，它叫捕梦网，所以我想它大概是用来捕捉噩梦的吧，不过它好像没起多大作用。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah?
Have you had some bad dreams lately?
sentences.zh: 你最近做了什么噩梦吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I've had some last night.
Really?
What did you dream about last night?
I don't even really remember.
Yeah, I always forget my dreams, too.
sentences.zh: 对啊，我也总是忘掉自己的梦。

sentences.en: I try sometimes to write them down so I can remember them.
sentences.zh: 我有时会试着把它们写下来，这样就能记住了。

sentences.en: Do you ever do that?
Um, no, ma'am.
I'm still working on spelling, so...
Gotcha.
That makes sense.
The New York Times, I'm Marco Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 这里是《纽约时报》，我是马尔科·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: Okay, that would probably be really hard to say Marco Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 好吧，要说出“马尔科·巴巴罗”这个名字可能真的挺难的。

sentences.en: I don't know.
Is that his last name, Marco Barbaro?
sentences.zh: 那是他的姓吗，马尔科·巴巴罗？

sentences.en: Barbaro, yeah.
Oh.
Yeah.
So, why don't we try it?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们为什么不试试呢？

sentences.en: Okay.
For the New York Times, I'm Ella.
sentences.zh: 为《纽约时报》报道，我是艾拉。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
Kids edition.
Today.
We are talking about fears and how to face them.
sentences.zh: 我们来聊聊恐惧以及如何面对恐惧。

sentences.en: It's Sunday, September 29th.
Hello.
Hello.
Michael.
Hi, is this Ella?
Um, that was my mom talking, but now it's me.
sentences.zh: 呃，刚才是我妈妈在说话，不过现在是我了。

sentences.en: Is that Michael?
Hi, Ella.
Hi.
Are you wearing headphones?
How does it feel?
Great.
All right, cool.
And then...
My colleague, Julia Longoria, traveled to Nashville, Tennessee, to record our conversation with Ella Maynors and her mother, Katie Maynors.
sentences.zh: 我的同事朱莉娅·隆戈里亚前往田纳西州纳什维尔，录制了我们与艾拉·梅诺尔斯及其母亲凯蒂·梅诺尔斯的对话。

sentences.en: It feels okay?
Yes, sir.
Are you calling me sir?
Yeah, sir.
You don't have to do that.
I appreciate it, but...
Got it.
Okay.
How are you hearing me through this microphone?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么通过这个麦克风听到我说话的？

sentences.en: I'm not actually hearing you through the microphone.
sentences.zh: 其实我不是通过麦克风听到你声音的。

sentences.en: I'm hearing you through the phone, but then eventually a lot of people are going to hear you through the microphone.
sentences.zh: 我是通过电话听到你声音的，但最终很多人会通过麦克风听到你的声音。

sentences.en: I don't get it.
Yeah, I don't get it either.
I thought that we might begin with just a couple of really basic questions.
sentences.zh: 我想我们可以从几个非常基础的问题开始。

sentences.en: How old are you?
I just turned nine.
And since you're in, Ella, your bedroom?
sentences.zh: 既然你在……艾拉，这是你的卧室吗？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
I wonder if you could describe a little bit of your surroundings, just a couple of things in that room that mean something to you.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能否描述一下你周边的环境，比如房间里对你有些意义的几样东西。

sentences.en: Um, everybody in here.
Mm-hmm.
My bunk bed and my stuffed animals.
sentences.zh: 我的双层床和我的毛绒玩具。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about those stuffed animals?
sentences.zh: 能跟我讲讲那些毛绒玩具吗？

sentences.en: I got a unicorn named Uni, and Bun Bun is my favorite, which is a bunny.
sentences.zh: 我有一个叫尤尼的独角兽，斑斑是我的最爱，它是一只兔子。

sentences.en: She has OCD.
Bun Bun has obsessive-compulsive disorder.
Yes, sir.
I mean, yes.
So, Ella, I know that you have been through a lot this last year, so I wanted to talk about that with you and with your mom.
sentences.zh: 所以，艾拉，我知道你这一年经历了很多，所以我想和你以及你妈妈聊聊这个。

sentences.en: Does that sound fine?
Yeah.
Let me start by asking you about your biggest fears.
sentences.zh: 让我先问问你最大的恐惧是什么。

sentences.en: What are you most scared of?
Um, throwing up, tornadoes, fires, wind decks, um, monsters, and going upstairs by myself or in the garage.
sentences.zh: 呃，呕吐、龙卷风、火灾、狂风，呃，怪物，还有独自上楼或者去车库。

sentences.en: And among those, because that's a fair number of fears, what would you say are the biggest, the things that you're most afraid of?
sentences.zh: 在这些之中——因为恐惧确实挺多的——你觉得哪几个最大，是你最害怕的事情？

sentences.en: Getting sick.
And, like, tornadoes.
We have, like, tornado watches here.
sentences.zh: 我们这里经常会有龙卷风预警之类的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
And the worst thing is our tornado siren is right beside our house, so you can hear it, like, really clear.
sentences.zh: 最糟糕的是，我们的龙卷风警报器就在我们房子旁边，所以你能听得特别清楚。

sentences.en: Oh, and it's really loud.
Oh, my God.
It's a twisty.
It's a twisty.
It's like the apocalypse is coming.
sentences.zh: 就像世界末日要来了一样。

sentences.en: That's just kind of where her mind goes.
sentences.zh: 她的脑回路差不多就是这样。

sentences.en: But we have never had a tornado actually hit our house.
sentences.zh: 但实际上从来没有龙卷风真正袭击过我们的房子。

sentences.en: That's good.
Yes, sir.
Yes.
Obsessive compulsive disorder is not what I imagined it to be.
sentences.zh: 强迫症和我之前想象的不太一样。

sentences.en: I pictured mainly the compulsive side of OCD, hand washing over and over, checking locks, or things like that.
sentences.zh: 我以前主要想象的是强迫症的强迫行为方面，比如反复洗手、检查门锁或者诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And with Ella in particular, her OCD focuses more on the obsession, obsessive thoughts of vomiting, of tornadoes.
sentences.zh: 特别是对艾拉来说，她的强迫症更多地集中在强迫观念上，比如对呕吐、对龙卷风的强迫性想法。

sentences.en: Ella's compulsion is actually avoidance.
sentences.zh: 艾拉的强迫行为其实是回避。

sentences.en: She will do anything to avoid the situations where vomit, tornado could happen.
sentences.zh: 她会想尽一切办法去避免那些可能会发生呕吐或龙卷风的情境。

sentences.en: OCD is just something that telling you that scary things are going to happen to you.
sentences.zh: 强迫症就是某种告诉你可怕事情将会降临到你头上的东西。

sentences.en: It took what Ella had a fear of.
sentences.zh: 它抓住了艾拉害怕的东西。

sentences.en: Vomit, tornadoes.
And just made that fear just enormous.
sentences.zh: 然后把那种恐惧无限放大。

sentences.en: When I found out that I had OCD, I feel like it changed my life a lot.
sentences.zh: 当我发现自己得了强迫症时，我觉得我的生活发生了很大的改变。

sentences.en: How so?
It was harder for me to do a lot of different stuff that other people can do.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，做很多别人能做到的不同事情变得更难了。

sentences.en: And it was just harder, I feel like.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得就是更难了。

sentences.en: The first time, it was just your typical school day.
sentences.zh: 第一次发作时，那只是一个普通的上学日。

sentences.en: And I get to the carpool line at school, and I drive up.
sentences.zh: 我到了学校的拼车接送车队，把车开了过去。

sentences.en: And instead of Ella walking to our car, her teacher does.
sentences.zh: 但不是艾拉朝我们的车走来，而是她的老师走了过来。

sentences.en: And I kind of rolled down the window, a little confused, going like, okay, where's Ella?
sentences.zh: 我摇下车窗，有点困惑，心想：好吧，艾拉呢？

sentences.en: And that's when she told me,
sentences.zh: 也就是在那时她告诉我，

sentences.en: Ella won't leave the classroom.
And of course, I'm going, what do you mean she won't leave the classroom?
sentences.zh: 当然，我当时就在想：她怎么会不肯离开教室呢？

sentences.en: And when I got to her classroom, she was literally, I just remember I was like screaming on the floor.
sentences.zh: 当我走到她的教室时，她简直……我只记得当时我在地板上尖叫。

sentences.en: If I moved, I was going to get sick.
sentences.zh: 如果我动一下，我就会生病。

sentences.en: Knees up to her chest, arms wrapped around her.
sentences.zh: 膝盖紧紧贴着胸口，双臂环抱自己。

sentences.en: She was tucked into a little ball.
And she was just laying on the floor, crying.
sentences.zh: 然后她就趴在地板上哭泣。

sentences.en: And she was able to say, like, if I move, I think I'm going to get sick.
sentences.zh: 她还能说出来，比如：如果我动了，我想我要生病了。

sentences.en: Or if I stand up,
I'm going to get sick.
There was not one thing I could say, you're going to be okay.
sentences.zh: 当时没有任何一句话能让我对她说“你会没事的”。

sentences.en: You know, you're not going to get sick.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，“你不会生病的”。

sentences.en: I am going to get sick.
That helped her.
I am going to get sick.
She was just stuck.
sentences.zh: 她整个人就卡在那里了。

sentences.en: I am going to get sick.
Her brain was stuck.
I am going to get sick.
On this one thought of, I'm going to get sick.
sentences.zh: 满脑子都是这同一个念头：我要生病了。

sentences.en: Ella was basically paralyzed with her fear.
sentences.zh: 艾拉基本上被她的恐惧吓得动弹不得。

sentences.en: And I ended up just having to literally pull her off the floor and carry her to my car.
sentences.zh: 最后我只好硬生生地把她从地板上拉起来，抱进我的车里。

sentences.en: I am going to get sick.
We didn't know that the things we were doing, the reassuring her, you know, you're not going to get sick.
sentences.zh: 我们当时并不知道我们所做的事情——那些对她的安慰，你知道的，“你不会生病的”——

sentences.en: Those were really amplifying her OCD.
sentences.zh: 其实是在极大地助长她的强迫症。

sentences.en: And the next thing that really pushed us was the day we got the phone call from the principal that told me there had been just a routine tornado drill at school.
sentences.zh: 接下来真正推了我们一把的事，是我们接到校长电话的那天，校长告诉我学校刚刚进行了一次例行的龙卷风演习。

sentences.en: Ella, can you tell me what happened that day?
sentences.zh: 艾拉，你能告诉我那天发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Well, it was cold outside, so I was wearing two jackets.
sentences.zh: 嗯，外面很冷，所以我穿了两件夹克。

sentences.en: The tornado drill was at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 龙卷风演习是在快放学的时候进行的。

sentences.en: Hearing the siren really just kind of sent Ella into that state of all-consuming fear.
sentences.zh: 听到警报声真的让艾拉陷入了那种被恐惧吞噬的状态。

sentences.en: I was telling myself, like, no, I'm not going to get sick.
sentences.zh: 我当时在心里对自己说，不，我不会生病的。

sentences.en: So you kind of tried to talk yourself out of it.
sentences.zh: 所以你当时试图说服自己不要去想它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
And I didn't take the two coats off.
sentences.zh: 而且我没有把那两件外套脱掉。

sentences.en: And it was, like, really hot inside.
And it was really thick coats.
sentences.zh: 而且那些外套真的很厚。

sentences.en: And we had to duck our heads down, even though it was just fake.
sentences.zh: 而且我们不得不把头低下去，尽管这只是假的。

sentences.en: We were to just make sure we knew what to do.
sentences.zh: 我们只是要确保我们知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: And what did you do?
I went to the bathroom with everybody.
sentences.zh: 我和大家一起去了洗手间。

sentences.en: We ducked our head in.
And, like, then, um, and then I threw up.
I mean, when they told me, it was like, oh, my gosh, like, poor child.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当他们告诉我的时候，我就觉得，天哪，这孩子真可怜。

sentences.en: How much worse could it get?
It had to be a tornado.
And it had to be vomit.
sentences.zh: 而且那一定是一堆呕吐物。

sentences.en: It was her two worst fears in one.
sentences.zh: 这是她最害怕的两件事合二为一了。

sentences.en: And what did that experience do to your fears?
sentences.zh: 那次经历对你的恐惧有什么影响？

sentences.en: It just made them worse, really.
sentences.zh: 真的只是让它们变得更糟了。

sentences.en: These fears just kind of consumed her.
sentences.zh: 这些恐惧差不多吞噬了她。

sentences.en: They kind of consumed her life.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎吞噬了她的生活。

sentences.en: There have been some boys that bullied me before.
sentences.zh: 以前有些男孩欺负过我。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what kinds of things they would say?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我他们会说些什么样的话吗？

sentences.en: Somebody has said to me, like, you're not that good as, like, other people because you have OCD.
sentences.zh: 有人对我说，比如，你没有其他人那么优秀，因为你有强迫症。

sentences.en: Hmm.
That's horrible.
I started crying.
When you start to see her not be able to do the things that she's been able to do,
sentences.zh: 当你开始看到她无法做到她以前能做的事情时，

sentences.en: is when, as a parent, you go, okay, we've really got to get on this.
sentences.zh: 作为一个父母，你就会想，好吧，我们真的得着手解决这件事了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
I realized that we had to do it the hard way.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我们必须用困难的方式来解决它。

sentences.en: What do you mean the hard way?
I don't really know.
What's up?
And a second, can, do you want to talk to yourself so I can have a break?
sentences.zh: 等一下，你可以，你想自己说一会儿话好让我休息一下吗？

sentences.en: Do you want a break, Ella?
Please.
Yeah, Ella, if you want a break, I would completely understand.
sentences.zh: 好吧，埃拉，如果你想休息，我完全理解。

sentences.en: Take a break.
Right now?
Yeah, go for it.
Okay.
Is your kid a cauliflower skeptic, bored by broccoli?
sentences.zh: 你的孩子对花椰菜持怀疑态度，对西兰花感到厌烦吗？

sentences.en: Sweetgreen and Schools and FoodCorps are on a mission to change that.
sentences.zh: Sweetgreen、Schools 和 FoodCorps 正在肩负改变这一现状的使命。

sentences.en: Together, they're working to reimagine school lunch and instill healthier eating habits in the 30 million students who rely on school lunch for daily nutrition.
sentences.zh: 他们正在共同努力重塑学校午餐，并在依赖学校午餐获取日常营养的 3000 万学生中培养更健康的饮食习惯。

sentences.en: With one million in funding to support FoodCorps hands-on learning and programmatic work in cafeterias,
sentences.zh: 凭借 100 万美元的资金支持 FoodCorps 在食堂开展的实践学习和项目工作，

sentences.en: Sweetgreen and Schools will introduce healthier, sustainable food to 22,000 elementary school students in America by the 2020 school year.
sentences.zh: Sweetgreen 和 Schools 将在 2020 学年之前为全美 22,000 名小学生引入更健康、可持续的食品。

sentences.en: Learn more at schools.sweetgreen.com.
Tell them you're ready.
Ready?
Yep.
Action.
Okay.
So once you determine that you have to do something.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你确定你必须做一件事。

sentences.en: Yes.
What do you do?
My husband and I, we just started researching.
sentences.zh: 我和我丈夫，我们开始做研究。

sentences.en: I did so much reading on OCD, the best treatment options for it.
sentences.zh: 我读了大量关于强迫症以及治疗它的最佳选择的书籍。

sentences.en: Ella just said too much and came to the conclusion that Ella needed some intense therapy.
sentences.zh: 埃拉说得太多了，最后得出结论，埃拉需要一些高强度的治疗。

sentences.en: So that's how we came across the Fear Facers camp that they put on two times a summer.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们偶然发现他们每年夏天举办两次的“勇面恐惧”夏令营的原因。

sentences.en: Fear Facers.
It is for children that have obsessive-compulsive disorder or other anxiety disorders.
sentences.zh: 它是为患有强迫症或其他焦虑症的儿童设立的。

sentences.en: It is put on by the University of Florida and...
sentences.zh: 它由佛罗里达大学主办，并且……

sentences.en: Sorry, Ella's making funny faces.
So Ella, just based on the name, it sounds like this is a place where kids go to confront their fears.
sentences.zh: 那么埃拉，仅凭这个名字，听起来这是一个孩子们去直面恐惧的地方。

sentences.en: Yes.
Okay, mom, stop talking.
It's my time to shine.
Sorry, Ella.
It's your time to shine.
Yeah.
Go for it.
Burn.
So Ella, tell me about what you first thought when you heard about this camp of Fear Facers.
sentences.zh: 那么埃拉，跟我讲讲你第一次听说这个“勇面恐惧”夏令营时的想法。

sentences.en: I was excited but nervous at the same time, and I was not ready for the drive.
sentences.zh: 我既兴奋又紧张，而且我还没准备好面对那段车程。

sentences.en: The drive.
Yes.
The long drive.
Yes.
Do you remember what you played on the radio?
sentences.zh: 你还记得你在收音机里放了什么吗？

sentences.en: Um, when I'm sad, I love hearing emotional songs, because I don't know why.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当我难过的时候，我喜欢听情感丰富的歌曲，因为我不知道为什么。

sentences.en: Like, call him Scott, you're the reason.
sentences.zh: 比如，叫他斯科特，你是我的理由。

sentences.en: And you are the reason that I'm still breathing.
sentences.zh: 而你是我依然在呼吸的理由。

sentences.en: I climb every night.
Ocean.
So we just arrived from Nashville to Gainesville.
sentences.zh: 所以我们刚从纳什维尔到达盖恩斯维尔。

sentences.en: As you arrived, can you describe what it looks like?
sentences.zh: 当你到达时，你能描述一下它看起来是什么样的吗？

sentences.en: There's tons of parking lots, and it wasn't a spend the night camp.
sentences.zh: 这里有大量的停车场，而且这不是一个过夜夏令营。

sentences.en: You should just look it up.
Okay, uh, let me do that.
Fear Facers Camp.
I'm looking for the photos.
There aren't really a lot of photos.
There really are almost no photos.
I could tell that it was like a really nice place.
sentences.zh: 我看得出来这是一个非常好的地方。

sentences.en: It kind of looked like a church.
sentences.zh: 它看起来有点像一座教堂。

sentences.en: So what was the first thing that you did when you got there?
sentences.zh: 那你到那里的第一件事是什么？

sentences.en: I got to meet my counselors, and I named my OCD O.C.
sentences.zh: 我见到了我的辅导员，我给我的强迫症起名叫 O.C。

sentences.en: O.C.?
And why did you do that?
I just like the name.
If you give that OCD a name, it helps them identify.
sentences.zh: 如果你给那个强迫症起个名字，它有助于他们识别。

sentences.en: Like, okay, is this me thinking, or me being scared, or is this OCD?
sentences.zh: 比如，好吧，这是我在思考，还是我在害怕，还是这是强迫症？

sentences.en: Or in Ellis' case, is this O.C.
sentences.zh: 或者在埃拉的例子中，这是 O.C.

sentences.en: being scared?
And tell me about O.C.
I always just picture him being like he's a bubble inside my brain.
sentences.zh: 我总是想象他就好像是我大脑里的一个气泡。

sentences.en: He's a little bubble blue.
It's blue, because blue's my favorite color.
sentences.zh: 它是蓝色的，因为蓝色是我最喜欢的颜色。

sentences.en: I don't know why.
So why did you give O.C.
sentences.zh: 那你觉得你为什么给 O.C.

sentences.en: your favorite color, do you think?
sentences.zh: 赋予你最喜欢的颜色呢？

sentences.en: I don't know.
Is it kind of like O.C.'s a little bit a part of you?
sentences.zh: 这有点像 O.C. 是你的一部分吗？

sentences.en: Like it's always going to be there?
sentences.zh: 就像它会永远存在一样？

sentences.en: Yeah, it would always be there.
She or he's just sneaky.
Sneaky?
Yeah.
Sneaky how?
You don't know what he's going to do.
